rules.sentence: A cardiomyopathy is a primary disorder of the heart muscle.

Manifestations of cardiomyopathies are usually those of heart failure and vary depending on whether there is systolic dysfunction, diastolic dysfunction, or both (. Some cardiomyopathies may also cause chest pain, syncope, or sudden death.
Evaluation typically includes ECG and echocardiography and sometimes MRI.
Treatment depends on the specific type and cause of cardiomyopathy (see .
Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is myocardial dysfunction causing heart failure in which ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction predominate.
Diagnosis is clinical and by chest x-ray and echocardiography.
Treatment is directed at the cause; if progressive and severe, heart transplantation may be needed.
The disorder affects both ventricles in most patients, only the left ventricle (LV) in a few (unless with an ischemic etiology), and only the right ventricle (RV) rarely.
